title: Suki secures $90M in series E funding to accelerate growth, expand AI capabilities
source_used: Healthcare Dive (own interview with chief executive Punit Soni)
key_facts: AI scribe company Suki raised $90 million in Series E financing as it expands beyond clinical documentation, clinical decision support and revenue cycle operations.
New investors Healthier Capital, Crosslink Capital and Hercules Capital joined existing investors.
Chief executive Punit Soni told Healthcare Dive the money will fund AI agents that complete post-visit tasks such as referrals and prior authorizations for new medications.
The money will also deepen ties with more than 30 health technology partners that embed Suki's tools, including Optum, Zoom and athenahealth.

Suki's tools include ambient listening and note creation, automated order entry, billing code suggestions and patient summaries; it recently launched Suki Ask, which answers clinical questions using patient charts and Wolters Kluwer's research database.
Rivals raised more last year: Ambience Healthcare $243 million and Abridge $300 million; Suki has raised more than $250 million over five rounds.
Soni said raising mega rounds of $100 million or more could create unreasonably high expectations.
quote_evidence: AI scribe company Suki has raised $90 million in Series E financing as it expands beyond clinical documentation, clinical decision-making support and revenue cycle operations.
The company now plans to build AI agents to complete tasks after the patient visit and treatment plan are completed, such as referrals and prior authorizations for new medications, Soni said.
Last year, Ambience Healthcare raised $243 million and Abridge secured $300 million
why_it_matters_hint: Doctors' note-taking AI is being extended into paperwork tasks that eat clinician time, but the new agents are planned, not shipped.
event_date: 13 Oct 2026 (Axios published the news first on the evening of 12 Oct US time)
